pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence contains only singular nouns? (1 mark)
   A. Girls carry baskets.
   B. The girl carries a basket.
   C. Many girls sing.
   D. The girls carry baskets.

2. What should you do before acting on a spoken instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Listen to all of it
   B. Move at once
   C. Laugh
   D. Look away

3. What is a good first step when reading for information? (1 mark)
   A. Close the book
   B. Guess the ending
   C. Copy the title
   D. Ask what you want to find out

4. Reading a text once for the general meaning is done (1 mark)
   A. never
   B. only with a partner
   C. first, before looking at details
   D. last, after everything

5. A sentence should begin with (1 mark)
   A. a capital letter
   B. a comma
   C. a small drawing
   D. a number

6. What is a gallery walk in handwriting practice? (1 mark)
   A. Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display
   B. A song
   C. A test of running
   D. A race in the field

7. Which is a good way to practise the shape of a letter? (1 mark)
   A. Trace it in the air with your finger
   B. Ignore it
   C. Rub it out
   D. Cover it

8. In Simon says, when should you obey an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Only when it begins with Simon says
   B. Only if you like it
   C. Never
   D. Always

9. Which words show the order of steps? (1 mark)
   A. first, then, next
   B. mother, father
   C. red, blue, green
   D. sun, rain

10. What is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A story about animals
   B. A type of poem
   C. A list of names
   D. Words that tell someone what to do

11. Which way of reading a sad part is best? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing
   B. Fast and loud
   C. Without pausing
   D. Slowly and softly

12. What does a comma tell a reader? (1 mark)
   A. To stop completely
   B. To take a short pause
   C. To shout
   D. To turn the page

13. Which sentence uses a comma correctly for speaking to someone? (1 mark)
   A. Wanjiku please, bring the umbrella
   B. Wanjiku please bring, the umbrella.
   C. Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.
   D. Wanjiku please bring the, umbrella.

14. Which sentence has the punctuation of a list correct? (1 mark)
   A. We wore, hats scarves and coats.
   B. We wore hats scarves, and coats
   C. We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   D. We wore hats scarves and coats.

15. What is a resource person? (1 mark)
   A. A person with special knowledge who visits to teach
   B. A kind of book
   C. A pupil who is late
   D. A bag for books

16. Which sentence needs a verb to be complete: Always ______ your hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. hands
   B. wash
   C. soap
   D. your

17. What do we do in a matching game with words? (1 mark)
   A. Draw a picture only
   B. Sing a song
   C. Match each word with its meaning
   D. Count the cards

18. What is the best way to read your part in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Read other people's lines
   B. Practise your lines with the right feeling
   C. Read it very quickly
   D. Never practise

19. Where can a class publish its final paragraphs? (1 mark)
   A. In a school or class magazine
   B. On a stone
   C. In the dustbin
   D. Under a bed

20. Which sentence has a verb? (1 mark)
   A. The red bag.
   B. Kamau washed his face.
   C. In the morning.
   D. Kamau and his face.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give the meaning of comprehension and say why it matters when we listen. (2 marks)

22. Give three signal words used to show the order of steps. (3 marks)

23. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about today's weather. Use at least one comma in a list, two capital letters for names and three full stops. (5 marks)

24. Explain what attentive listening means. (2 marks)

25. List three habits of an attentive listener. (3 marks)

26. List three ways of reading with expression. (3 marks)

27. Pick out the nouns in this song line: We roast the maize and boil the beans. (3 marks)

28. Give two sequence words. (2 marks)

29. Explain what a dialogue is. (2 marks)

30. What is a paragraph and what is its main idea? (2 marks)

31. Explain why sequencing ideas is important in writing. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — The girl carries a basket.
   Girl and basket each name one thing.

2. A — Listen to all of it
   Listening to the end helps you act correctly.

3. D — Ask what you want to find out
   A question in mind helps you look for the right facts.

4. C — first, before looking at details
   A first reading gives the main idea.

5. A — a capital letter
   Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

6. A — Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display
   Pupils view and comment on displayed work.

7. A — Trace it in the air with your finger
   Tracing helps the hand remember the movement.

8. A — Only when it begins with Simon says
   The game is about listening carefully.

9. A — first, then, next
   Sequence words show the order.

10. D — Words that tell someone what to do
   An instruction says what to do.

11. D — Slowly and softly
   A slow, soft voice matches sadness.

12. B — To take a short pause
   Commas show short pauses.

13. C — Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.
   A comma follows the name of the person addressed.

14. C — We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   A comma follows each item except the last two, which are joined by and.

15. A — A person with special knowledge who visits to teach
   A nurse visiting a class is an example of a resource person.

16. B — wash
   Wash is the action word that completes the sentence.

17. C — Match each word with its meaning
   The game links words to meanings.

18. B — Practise your lines with the right feeling
   Practice with expression helps fluency.

19. A — In a school or class magazine
   Publishing shares the writing.

20. B — Kamau washed his face.
   Washed is the verb.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Comprehension means understanding. It matters because we can then remember and use what we heard.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for why it matters.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, after that, finally (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example On Monday in Kisumu the sky was cloudy. It was cool, windy and dry. Amina wore a sweater.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence that is complete and correct, one for a comma in a list and one for correct capitals.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attentive listening means choosing to give your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker so that you understand and remember what is said.
   Working / marking points: One mark for choosing to pay attention and one mark for understanding or remembering.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Face the speaker, stay quiet, think about the words, wait for your turn, respond correctly (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each habit, up to three.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Change loudness, change speed, pause at punctuation, use different voices for characters, use face and hands.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: maize and beans (and we is a pronoun, not a noun)
   Working / marking points: One mark for maize, one mark for beans, and one mark for not including roast or boil, which are actions.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, finally (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people, shown with each speaker's name and words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for speakers.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: A paragraph is a group of sentences about one topic. The main idea is what it is mostly about.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

31. (3 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader follow the ideas, avoids confusion and makes writing logical.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each valid point.
